6→7: Native compiler (Project Corsa): tsc is rewritten in Go (tsgo), delivering roughly up to 10x faster type-checking and builds
`strict` is enabled by default when not explicitly set (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictFunctionTypes, ...)
Legacy `module` values removed (amd, umd, system, none); supported outputs are ESNext, ES2022, NodeNext, and CommonJS
No stable programmatic compiler API until 7.1 — tools that embed tsc (ts-loader, and Vue/Svelte/Angular template type-checking) should stay on 6.x until it lands

Stricter JSDoc-in-JS semantics: values can no longer stand in for types (use `typeof`), `@enum` is unrecognized, postfix `!` and Closure-style function syntax are unsupported, and `@class` no longer creates constructors
TypeScript 6.x was the bridge release that surfaced these changes as deprecation warnings before 7.0 made them hard errors
